approach: Generate both a light and dark color scheme from the same palette using mat.theme's color.theme-type option, and switch between them by toggling a class (or relying on prefers-color-scheme) on a root element rather than re-theming components individually.
explanation: mat.theme's color.theme-type option ('light', 'dark', or the default 'auto') controls which half of the derived M3 tonal palette is mapped onto the emitted --mat-sys-* custom properties. Scoping a second mat.theme include with theme-type: dark under a toggleable class lets every Material component pick up dark-mode colors automatically wherever that class applies, since components read the custom properties rather than hardcoding colors. theme-type: auto instead emits both light and dark values wrapped in a prefers-color-scheme media query directly, requiring no class toggle at all if following the OS setting exclusively is acceptable.
gotchas: Only one mat.theme scope should actually apply to a given element at a time — nesting both the light and dark mat.theme includes under selectors that can both match the same element (e.g. :root and html) applies both, and the later one in source order wins unpredictably.

theme-type: auto ties dark mode strictly to the OS-level prefers-color-scheme setting — a product that needs a manual, user-facing dark-mode toggle independent of the OS setting should use explicit light/dark theme-type values under a class instead.

Components that render into the CDK overlay container (dialogs, menus, autocomplete panels) are appended outside the component tree near the end of the document body — a class-based dark-mode toggle must be applied high enough (e.g. on html or body) to also cover the overlay container, or overlay-rendered content won't pick up the dark palette.
